note: Rewritten from Krishna & Araujo's 1968 redescription of the soldier of N. villosus; the fragment begins in the middle of the soldier description (the first line reads "ightly concave" in the OCR), so the anterior half of the head capsule and the first part of the labrum description are not included. The column headings of Table 20 are Lectotype / Paralectotype / Chaquimayo, Peru / Ecuador / Range, five columns in all, whereas the OCR gives only 4 values per row, so the correspondence between columns and values is uncertain; the measurements are reproduced in their original order without inference. Locality, type specimens and supplementary records are in the original, pp. 127-128.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Slightly concave at the tip, ending in a long, pointed apex; inner margin truncate (the subject of this sentence is missing because the fragment begins in mid-description); the postmentum expands in its anterior third, its sides converging toward the anterior margin and diverging toward the posterior margin. Pronotum width 0.52-0.65 of the head width; anterior lobe semicircular, erect, at almost a right angle to the posterior lobe; anterior margin with a shallow median concavity, posterior margin rounded. Metanotum about as wide as the pronotum, its posterior margin deeply and broadly concave. Measurements (mm, 5 soldiers, Table 20): head-capsule lateral length 4.80 / 5.30 / 4.90 / 5.50-5.70; maximum head width 3.30 / 3.50 / 3.18 / 3.80; maximum head height 2.20 / 2.58 / 2.10 / 2.60; left mandible length 3.80 / 4.60 / 3.85 / 4.50-4.60; right mandible length 3.50 / 4.40 / 3.50 / 4.10; maximum postmentum width 0.80 / 0.90 / 0.80 / 0.98-1.00; minimum postmentum width 0.50 / 0.70 / 0.45 / 0.55-0.58; postmentum length 3.30 / 3.20 / 2.70 / 3.40-3.50; pronotum mid-length 0.75 / 1.10 / 0.83 / 1.10; maximum pronotum length 0.83 / 1.20 / 0.85 / 1.10; maximum pronotum width 1.70 / 2.30 / 1.60 / 2.00; hindtibia length 2.96 / 2.95 / 2.90 / 3.00.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is closely related to N. utiariti (which occurs in central and northern Brazil). N. utiariti is larger in all measurements; its cephalic setae are smaller, stouter, brown and very conspicuous; the labrum is square, slightly longer than wide, and regularly trilobed; the antennal segments from 3 to 15 are swollen apically; the postmentum is not angulate at the tip, each lateral apical lobe bearing 2 setae; the fore coxa has a more sclerotized ridge, its anterior margin with dense, coarse, stiff setae, and many similar setae regularly scattered on its inner face; the anterior and posterior lobes of the pronotum do not form a wide angle; many small, stiff setae are scattered on the inner face of the cervical sclerite.
